description: Covers excretion versus egestion, the roles of the kidneys, lungs, skin and liver, the structure and function of the nephron, urine formation through filtration and reabsorption, and clinical links such as dialysis and diabetes.

mcq.questionText: Excretion is defined as the removal of:

options.text: Metabolic waste products from the body

mcq.explanation: Excretion removes waste made by the body's own metabolism, such as carbon dioxide and urea. Exam Tip: Excretion (metabolic waste) differs from egestion (undigested food).

mcq.questionText: The main organs of excretion in the human body include the kidneys, lungs, skin and:
mcq.explanation: The liver also excretes waste through urea formation and the production of bile pigments. Exam Tip: Excretory organs: kidneys (urine), lungs (CO2), skin (sweat), liver (urea, bile pigments).

mcq.questionText: The kidneys remove waste from the blood mainly in the form of:
mcq.explanation: Kidneys filter blood to produce urine, which contains urea. Exam Tip: Urea is the main nitrogenous waste, formed in the liver.

mcq.questionText: The functional unit of the kidney, responsible for filtering blood, is called the:
mcq.explanation: The nephron is the functional and filtering unit of the kidney. Exam Tip: Each kidney has about a million nephrons.

mcq.questionText: The tube that carries urine from each kidney to the bladder is called the:
mcq.explanation: The ureter is the tube that carries urine from each kidney down to the bladder. Exam Tip: Ureter (kidney to bladder) vs urethra (bladder to outside).

mcq.questionText: The tube that carries urine from the bladder to the outside of the body is called the:
mcq.explanation: The urethra carries urine from the bladder to outside the body. Exam Tip: Urethra ends the pathway.

mcq.questionText: The organ that temporarily stores urine before it is released from the body is the:
mcq.explanation: The bladder temporarily stores urine before it is released from the body. Exam Tip: The bladder stretches to hold urine.

mcq.questionText: The waste gas removed from the body through the lungs is:
mcq.explanation: Carbon dioxide, a waste product of respiration, is exhaled through the lungs. Exam Tip: Lungs excrete CO2 and some water vapour.

mcq.questionText: The skin excretes excess water and salts mainly in the form of:
mcq.explanation: Sweat glands release excess water and salts from the skin. Exam Tip: Sweating also helps cool the body.

mcq.questionText: Urea, a major nitrogenous waste product, is formed in the:
mcq.explanation: The liver converts excess amino acids into urea. Exam Tip: Liver MAKES urea; kidneys REMOVE it.

mcq.questionText: In the nephron, the process by which blood is forced through a network of capillaries to filter out small molecules is called:
mcq.explanation: Filtration occurs in the glomerulus, forcing blood through capillaries to push small molecules into the tubule. Exam Tip: Filtration pushes small molecules into the nephron tubule.

mcq.questionText: The process by which useful substances such as glucose and water are taken back into the blood from the nephron tubule is called:
mcq.explanation: Reabsorption returns useful substances such as glucose and water into the blood from the nephron tubule. Exam Tip: Reabsorption recovers glucose, most water, some salts.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is NOT normally reabsorbed and remains in the urine?
mcq.explanation: Urea is a waste product that is not reabsorbed and remains in the urine. Exam Tip: Glucose and most water/salts are reabsorbed; urea is not.

mcq.questionText: A person with kidney failure may need a treatment that filters waste from their blood using a machine, called:
mcq.explanation: Dialysis uses a machine to filter waste from the blood when the kidneys cannot. Exam Tip: A medical application directly linked to nephron function.

mcq.questionText: The presence of glucose in a person's urine may be a sign of the disease:
mcq.explanation: High blood glucose exceeds the kidney's reabsorption capacity, so glucose appears in urine, a sign of diabetes. Exam Tip: Testing urine for glucose is a simple diagnostic clue for diabetes.

fib.questionText: The removal of metabolic waste products from the body is called ____.
fib.explanation: Excretion is the removal of metabolic waste products from the body, unlike egestion which removes undigested food. Exam Tip: Excretion != egestion.

fib.questionText: The functional unit of the kidney that filters blood is the ____.
fib.explanation: The nephron is the functional and filtering unit of the kidney. Exam Tip: Millions of nephrons per kidney.

fib.questionText: The tube carrying urine from the kidney to the bladder is the ____.
fib.explanation: The ureter connects each kidney to the bladder, carrying urine down to it. Exam Tip: One ureter per kidney.

fib.questionText: The tube carrying urine from the bladder to outside the body is the ____.
fib.explanation: The urethra carries urine from the bladder to outside the body. Exam Tip: Do not confuse with ureter.

fib.questionText: The organ that stores urine temporarily is the ____.
fib.explanation: The bladder stores urine temporarily before it leaves the body. Exam Tip: The bladder stretches to hold urine.

fib.questionText: Urea is formed in the ____ from excess amino acids.
fib.explanation: The liver forms urea by breaking down excess amino acids. Exam Tip: Liver makes urea; kidneys remove it.

fib.questionText: The process of forcing small molecules out of the blood into the nephron is called ____.
fib.explanation: Filtration forces small molecules out of the blood into the nephron tubule at the glomerulus. Exam Tip: Happens in the glomerulus.

fib.questionText: The process by which useful substances are taken back into the blood from the nephron is called ____.
fib.explanation: Reabsorption returns useful substances like glucose and water back into the blood. Exam Tip: Glucose and water are reabsorbed; urea is not.

fib.questionText: The gas excreted by the lungs as a waste product of respiration is ____.
fib.explanation: Carbon dioxide is a waste gas produced during respiration and excreted via the lungs. Exam Tip: CO2 is breathed out continuously.

fib.questionText: The presence of glucose in urine may indicate the disease ____.
fib.explanation: Glucose appearing in urine may indicate diabetes, since normal reabsorption should remove all glucose. Exam Tip: A simple urine test can hint at diabetes.

tf.questionText: Excretion is the removal of metabolic waste products from the body.
tf.explanation: Excretion covers waste such as carbon dioxide, urea, sweat and bile pigments produced by the body's own metabolism. Exam Tip: Includes CO2, urea, sweat, bile pigments.

tf.questionText: Egestion and excretion mean exactly the same thing.
tf.explanation: Egestion is the removal of undigested food, while excretion is the removal of metabolic waste; they are not the same process. Exam Tip: This distinction is heavily tested.

tf.questionText: The kidneys are the only organs involved in excretion.
tf.explanation: The lungs, skin and liver also perform excretion alongside the kidneys. Exam Tip: Lungs, skin and liver also excrete.

tf.questionText: The nephron is the functional unit of the kidney.
tf.explanation: The nephron carries out filtration and reabsorption, making it the kidney's functional unit. Exam Tip: Performs filtration and reabsorption.

tf.questionText: The ureter carries urine from the bladder to outside the body.
tf.explanation: The urethra carries urine outward from the bladder; the ureter carries urine from the kidney to the bladder. Exam Tip: The urethra carries it outward; ureter is kidney to bladder.

tf.questionText: Urea is formed in the liver from the breakdown of excess amino acids.
tf.explanation: The liver breaks down excess amino acids into urea, linking excretion to protein metabolism. Exam Tip: Links excretion to protein metabolism.

tf.questionText: Glucose is normally reabsorbed back into the blood in a healthy person.
tf.explanation: In a healthy person, all filtered glucose is reabsorbed back into the blood; its presence in urine is abnormal. Exam Tip: Glucose in urine is abnormal, may signal diabetes.

tf.questionText: Urea is fully reabsorbed back into the blood after filtration.
tf.explanation: Urea is a waste product and is not reabsorbed; it remains in the urine. Exam Tip: Urea is a waste, not reabsorbed.

tf.questionText: Dialysis is a treatment that artificially filters waste from the blood when the kidneys fail.
tf.explanation: Dialysis machines filter waste from the blood, substituting for failed kidney function. Exam Tip: A real medical application of nephron understanding.

tf.questionText: Sweat, released by the skin, contains excess water and salts.
tf.explanation: Sweat carries excess water and salts out through the skin. Exam Tip: Links to temperature regulation.

summary.correctAnswer: Excretion is the removal of metabolic waste products made by the body (such as urea and carbon dioxide), while egestion is the removal of undigested food material from the gut.
summary.explanation: These two processes are often confused but refer to different types of waste leaving the body. Exam Tip: Excretion = metabolic waste; egestion = undigested food.

summary.correctAnswer: The kidneys, lungs, skin and liver, which together remove different waste products from the body.
summary.explanation: Each organ excretes a specific waste: kidneys remove urine, lungs remove carbon dioxide, skin removes sweat, and the liver processes urea and bile pigments. Exam Tip: Remember all four organs, not just the kidneys.

summary.correctAnswer: The functional unit of the kidney, responsible for filtering blood and forming urine through filtration and reabsorption.
summary.explanation: Each kidney contains about a million nephrons working to clean the blood. Exam Tip: Each kidney has about a million nephrons.

summary.correctAnswer: The ureter is the tube carrying urine from each kidney to the bladder; the urethra is the tube carrying urine from the bladder to outside the body.
summary.explanation: These two tubes are easily confused, but the ureter comes before the bladder and the urethra comes after it. Exam Tip: Ureter (kidney to bladder), urethra (bladder to outside).

summary.correctAnswer: The organ that temporarily stores urine before it is released from the body.
summary.explanation: The bladder stretches to hold urine until it is convenient to urinate. Exam Tip: The bladder stretches to hold urine.

summary.correctAnswer: The process in which the liver converts excess amino acids into urea, a nitrogenous waste product later removed by the kidneys.
summary.explanation: The liver makes urea, but the kidneys are responsible for removing it from the blood. Exam Tip: Liver MAKES urea; kidneys REMOVE it.

summary.correctAnswer: The process in the nephron where blood is forced through capillaries in the glomerulus, pushing small molecules like water, glucose, salts and urea into the tubule.
summary.explanation: Filtration is the first step of urine formation in the nephron. Exam Tip: Filtration pushes small molecules into the nephron tubule.

summary.correctAnswer: The process by which useful substances such as glucose, most water and some salts are taken back into the blood from the nephron tubule.
summary.explanation: Reabsorption follows filtration and prevents useful substances from being lost in urine. Exam Tip: Reabsorption recovers glucose, most water, some salts.

summary.correctAnswer: A medical treatment that uses a machine to filter waste products from the blood when the kidneys fail.
summary.explanation: Dialysis acts as an artificial nephron, passing blood next to a fluid across a membrane so waste can move out. Exam Tip: A medical application directly linked to nephron function.

summary.correctAnswer: The presence of glucose in urine, which occurs when blood glucose is too high for the nephron to fully reabsorb, a sign of diabetes.
summary.explanation: Testing urine for glucose is a simple way to screen for diabetes. Exam Tip: Testing urine for glucose is a simple diagnostic clue for diabetes.

hoq.questionText: A patient's urine test finds glucose present, with high thirst and frequent urination. Explain using nephron knowledge and name the probable condition.

options.text: The kidneys are producing too much urea
The blood glucose level is too high, so not all glucose can be reabsorbed in the nephron, and the excess appears in the urine - a sign of diabetes
The liver has stopped working completely

hoq.explanation: Normal reabsorption removes all glucose. High blood glucose overwhelms reabsorption capacity, leaving glucose in urine, a sign of diabetes. Exam Tip: Presence of glucose in urine means reabsorption has been overwhelmed by high blood sugar.

hoq.questionText: Explain step by step how the nephron converts blood into urine, using filtration and reabsorption.

options.text: Blood is filtered once and nothing more happens

Blood is filtered at the glomerulus (removing small molecules like water, glucose, salts and urea into the tubule); then useful substances (glucose, most water, some salts) are reabsorbed back into the blood, leaving urine containing water, urea and some salts
Urine is made directly without any filtering

hoq.explanation: Filtration at the glomerulus removes small molecules; reabsorption returns useful substances; what remains becomes urine. Exam Tip: Filtration always comes first, then reabsorption selectively returns what the body needs.

hoq.questionText: A kidney failure patient is connected to a dialysis machine. Explain how dialysis functions as an artificial nephron.

options.text: Dialysis adds more urea to the blood

Dialysis passes the patient's blood alongside a fluid across a membrane, allowing waste products like urea to move out of the blood (similar to filtration in a nephron), before returning the cleaned blood to the body
Dialysis replaces the need for a bladder
Dialysis has no relation to kidney function

hoq.explanation: Dialysis mimics filtration - blood passes next to a fluid across a membrane, waste moves out, cleaned blood returns. Exam Tip: Dialysis substitutes for the filtration role of the nephron when kidneys fail.
